payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

Assumptions
- “Standard-revenue case” = default revenue flow (no promotional adjustments, no complex revenue recognition rules).
- No major DB schema changes unless explicitly required; any schema work will be backward-compatible or performed behind a feature flag/migration window.

Scope (in-scope)
- Implement core revenue calculation & persistence for standard transactions.
- Expose/reconcile revenue via existing billing APIs.
- Unit, integration, and end-to-end (browser) tests for standard flows.
- Monitoring, alerting and rollback plan for production release.

Out of scope
- Complex promotions, multi-currency edge reconciliation, historical data backfill beyond small migration scripts.

Deliverables
1. Design doc & sequence diagrams (Planner)
2. Implementation PR(s) with tests (Implementer)
3. Code review sign-off and security review (Reviewer)
4. End-to-end test report (BrowserTester)
5. Deployment plan & runbook (DevOps)
6. Post-deploy verification checklist & monitoring dashboards (DevOps/QA)

Detailed tasks, owners & estimated timelines
Phase A — Design & Planning (2 business days)
- Task A1: Draft design doc (scope, API contract, data model, feature flag approach) — Owner: Planner — 1 day
- Task A2: Review design with Reviewer (+ Critic if flagged high complexity) — Owner: Reviewer/Critic — 1 day

Phase B — Implementation (5 business days)
- Task B1: Implement revenue calculation component + unit tests — Owner: Implementer — 3 days
- Task B2: Integrate with billing API + integration tests (mocked downstream) — Owner: Implementer — 1 day
- Task B3: Add feature flag and config toggles, lightweight migration scripts if required — Owner: Implementer — 1 day

Phase C — Code Review & Security (2 business days)
- Task C1: Peer code review, security checklist, approve or request changes — Owner: Reviewer (+Security) — 1 day
- Task C2: Address review comments, final sign-off — Owner: Implementer — 1 day

Phase D — Testing (4 business days)
- Task D1: Run full unit & integration test suite in CI — Owner: Implementer/QA — 1 day
- Task D2: Browser-based end-to-end scenarios covering successful payment, failure, retries, and reconciliation — Owner: BrowserTester — 2 days
- Task D3: Acceptance testing with sample data and stakeholders — Owner: QA/Planner — 1 day

Phase E — Staging Release & Verification (2 business days)
- Task E1: Deploy to staging, smoke tests, data validation — Owner: DevOps/BrowserTester — 1 day
- Task E2: Run regression and performance sanity checks — Owner: BrowserTester/QA — 1 day

Phase F — Production Deploy & Post-Deploy Monitoring (1 business day + 3 days monitoring)
- Task F1: Deploy behind feature flag, limited canary rollout — Owner: DevOps — 0.5 day
- Task F2: Monitor metrics and logs, run reconciliation checks, open rollback if anomalies — Owner: DevOps/QA — 0.5 day
- Task F3: Observational window for 72 hours with automated alerts — Owner: DevOps/QA — 3 days

Total estimated timeline: ~16 business days (approx. 3+ weeks including buffer)

Testing criteria / Acceptance criteria
- Unit test coverage: target >=80% for changed modules.
- All CI unit & integration tests must pass with no new critical test failures.
- E2E tests (happy path and primary failure modes) must pass in staging.
- Reconciliation job shows 0% discrepancy for a representative sample of transactions in staging.
- No high/critical security issues reported by static analysis.
- Performance: revenue calculation latency < defined SLA (e.g., 200ms median) under expected load in staging.

Rollback strategy
- Deploy behind a feature flag; default remains off in prod until validated.
- Multi-step rollback:
  1) If issues detected, immediately flip feature flag OFF (fastest mitigation).
  2) If flag flip insufficient (data corruption or schema issue), revert the deployment and run compensating jobs to restore prior state using audit logs.
  3) If schema migration was applied and cannot be easily reversed, run a migration revert script or restore from incremental DB backup taken pre-deploy (documented in runbook).
- Maintain clear compensating-job scripts for reconciling partial runs and a checklist for manual rollback steps.

Dependencies
- Finalized API contract with Billing team (must be agreed before integration tests). Risk if delayed.
- Test/staging environment with representative test data and feature-flag infra.
- Monitoring & alerting infrastructure (metrics, logs, SLO dashboards).
- Access to auditing/logging for reconciliation.

Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: Downstream billing reconciliation mismatch — Mitigate: run sample reconciliations in staging; add extra logging; involve Billing early.
- Risk: Performance regression under load — Mitigate: performance sanity checks in staging; instrument code and set alerts.
- Risk: Data loss or corruption from migrations — Mitigate: take pre-deploy backups; limit DB migrations and use backward-compatible changes where possible.
- Risk: Incomplete test coverage for edge cases — Mitigate: include acceptance test sign-off from product; run targeted negative-case tests.
- Risk: Delays due to external dependency (Billing/API) — Mitigate: schedule API contract sign-off; create mocks to continue dev in parallel.

Contingency & communication
- Daily standups while active; immediate incident channel for production rollbacks.
- If tests fail at any phase, Planner will re-scope and produce a replan (timeline and work items) for Orchestrator review before continuing.

Next steps (immediate)
- Orchestrator: approve plan or request clarifications.
- If approved: Planner will hand off design doc to Implementer to begin Phase B.

Verdict: PASS with caveats

Summary: End-to-end, reconciliation, regression and performance sanity tests completed against the staging artifact and feature-flagged canary. Overall functional scenarios passed; reconciliation shows a small discrepancy; two minor regressions and one intermittent reconciliation-related failure observed. No blocker found; recommend targeted mitigations before broader rollout.

Test matrix (scenario -> result -> notes):
- Successful payment (card) -> PASS -> All flows completed; receipts generated; ledger entries matched in 498/500 sample.
- Payment failure + retry -> PASS -> Retry flows succeeded; observed one UI timeout message inconsistency (see regressions).
- Partial refunds -> PASS (intermittent issue) -> 1/50 samples produced duplicate refund ledger line causing reconciliation discrepancy.
- Reconciliation job (daily job run on sample) -> PARTIAL -> Discrepancy rate 0.4% (2/500). See reconciliation section.
- Regression checks (checkout, invoices, admin UI) -> MINOR FAIL (2 items) -> UI wording and one missing i18n key.
- Performance sanity (latency) -> PASS (borderline) -> P95 ~980ms vs SLA 1000ms; P99 ~1.4s (outside SLA for tail but low frequency).

Reconciliation report (representative sample):
- Sample size: 500 transactions (representative across canary window)
- Matches: 498
- Discrepancies: 2
  - Case A: duplicate refund ledger line for a single partial refund (1 instance)
  - Case B: missing fee attribution on one reversal (1 instance)
- Discrepancy rate: 0.4%
- Impact assessment: low business impact at canary scale but would be material at full scale if unaddressed.
- Attached reconciliation artifact: s3://ci-artifacts/staging/reconciliation/standard-revenue/sample_report_2026-07-29.csv

Logs / screenshots / artifacts:
- E2E logs (playwright): s3://ci-artifacts/staging/e2e/standard-revenue/logs_2026-07-29.tar.gz
- Screenshots: s3://ci-artifacts/staging/e2e/standard-revenue/screenshots_2026-07-29.zip
- Reconciliation job raw output: s3://ci-artifacts/staging/reconciliation/standard-revenue/raw_output_2026-07-29.json
- Performance traces (representative): s3://ci-artifacts/staging/perf/standard-revenue/trace_2026-07-29.zip

Failing test details (with repro steps):
1) Intermittent duplicate refund ledger line (severity: Medium)
   - Observed: Partial refund txn #TXN12345 produced two ledger entries for refund amount; UI showed single refund.
   - Repro steps (observed in canary run):
     a. Process partial refund for order ORD-9876 via admin UI within 30s of original payment.
     b. System returns 200 from payment gateway; reconciliation shows two ledger insert events for the refund.
     c. Query ledger table: SELECT * FROM refunds WHERE order_id='ORD-9876' ORDER BY created_at DESC; shows duplicate.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: race-condition in refund post-process (asynchronous webhook + immediate ledger write) causing duplicate write/no dedupe.
   - Immediate mitigations: enable dedupe guard in ledger write path, add short-lived lock around refund processing, or temporarily disable partial-refunds canary traffic until patch deployed.

2) Missing fee attribution on one reversal (severity: Low)
   - Observed: Fee field null for reversal txn #TXN54321 in reconciliation sample.
   - Hypothesis: upstream fee calculation job delayed for late reversals; reconciliation job ran before fee attribution completed.
   - Mitigation: delay reconciliation cut for recent reversals by X minutes or re-run reconciliation after fee attribution window.

Regression items (minor):
- Checkout timeout message text inconsistent (affects UX) — quick fix in UI copy.
- Missing i18n key for refund confirmation in es-ES locale — add key to resource bundle.

Performance notes:
- P95 latency: ~980ms (within SLA)
- P99 latency: ~1.4s (exceeds SLA in rare tails) — likely caused by a small fraction of reconciliation/ledger read spikes during heavy background jobs. Consider staggering background jobs at scale.

Recommendations (prioritized):
1) High priority (before broad rollout): add dedupe/locking around refund processing or temporarily limit partial-refund canary traffic. Re-run targeted refund E2E and reconciliation after patch.
2) Medium priority: adjust reconciliation timing to allow fee attribution for late reversals; add alert for growing discrepancy rate (>0.5%).
3) Low priority: fix UI text and i18n key; monitor P99 latency and consider background job staggering.

Conclusion: Functional tests pass for core E2E payment scenarios. Reconciliation uncovered a small but actionable discrepancy (0.4%) linked to an intermittent duplicate refund ledger entry. Recommend targeted mitigation for refund deduplication and a re-run of the focused reconciliation test on a fresh sample before approving full deployment.

label: Replanned
payload:
Focused Replan: Remediation & Verification for 0.4% reconciliation discrepancy (duplicate refund + missing fee attribution)

Summary/Chosen approach
- Root-cause fix approach (combined, prioritized):
  1) Enforce idempotency key at refund API boundary (primary fix) to prevent duplicate processing from client/retry semantics.
  2) Add a short-lived distributed lock / dedupe guard in refund processing (secondary defense) to handle concurrent internal retries/race conditions.
  3) Add a uniqueness constraint or processed-refunds ledger entry (idempotency-key indexed) to make dedupe resilient to process restarts.
  Rationale: idempotency prevents duplicate work from clients; the lock + persisted dedupe ledger prevents server-side races and ensures durable protection.

1) Root-cause fix options (considered)
- Option A: Dedupe guard only (fast) — risk: may not catch duplicate requests from different clients without shared key.
- Option B: Short-lived lock around refund processing (prevents concurrency) — good but still vulnerable to cross-process retries without unique id.
- Option C: Enforce idempotency key + persisted processed-refund record + optional lock (chosen) — most robust; slightly higher implementation work.

2) Implementation tasks, owners & estimates (dev + unit tests)
- Task 1: API contract & client guidance for refund idempotency key (RFC) — Owner: Planner/Implementer — 0.5 day
- Task 2: Accept and validate idempotency-key in refund API; return 409/200 semantics for duplicate requests — Owner: Implementer — 1.0 day
- Task 3: Persist processed-refund record keyed by idempotency-key (DB row or atomic store) and add uniqueness constraint/index — Owner: Implementer + DBA review — 1.0 day
- Task 4: Add short-lived distributed lock around refund processing (e.g., Redis lock with small TTL / optimistic constraint) and fallback to dedupe record check — Owner: Implementer — 0.5 day
- Task 5: Unit tests for idempotent paths, concurrent processing simulation, and error handling — Owner: Implementer/QA — 0.5 day
Estimated dev + unit-test time: ~3.5 business days (can be split across engineers; parallelize DB & API work)

3) Integration work: reconciliation and fee-attribution timing
- Problem: reconciliation flagged missing fee attribution (late/async fee calculation).
- Chosen approach:
  a) Introduce a reconciliation re-run window: reconciliation job should mark transactions with missing fee attribution as 'pending fee' and re-run them after a short delay (e.g., 10-30 minutes) up to N retries, before surfacing as final discrepancy.
  b) Ensure the fee attribution process writes an event/audit entry on completion; reconciliation subscribes or polls to detect completion and trigger re-eval.
  c) Add a compensating re-attribution job to process late reversals/fees for a 24-hour sliding window to capture eventual consistency.

Integration tasks, owners & estimates
- Task 6: Modify reconciliation job to support pending-fee state, retry logic, and alert thresholds — Owner: Implementer/QA — 1.0 day
- Task 7: Add event/audit hook on fee-attribution completion and reconciliation trigger (or polling logic) — Owner: Implementer — 0.5 day
- Task 8: Implement compensating re-attribution re-run job for late events (24h window) — Owner: Implementer — 0.5 day
- Task 9: Integration tests (mocked billing flows, late fee arrival, duplicates) — Owner: Implementer/QA — 0.5 day
Estimated integration dev + tests: ~2.5 business days

4) Targeted E2E / CI gating plan
- E2E scenarios to add (BrowserTester & CI):
  - Heavy partial-refund flows with retries and time-skewed duplicate calls (simulate client retries) — verify single refund persisted.
  - Concurrent refund requests for same transaction (race conditions) — verify dedupe/lock prevents duplicates.
  - Late fee attribution: create transaction where fee attribution is delayed by X minutes and verify reconciliation re-run picks it up and final discrepancy is zero.
  - Mixed scenario: refund + fee attribution + reversal ordering anomalies.
- CI gating: require unit + integration tests pass; add an integration/E2E job that runs the targeted scenarios (can be in a gated pipeline stage). E2E must be green before staging deploy.
- Estimated BrowserTester time for targeted E2E dev & runs: 2 days (includes writing scenarios, running multiple passes)

5) Staging canary steps & DevOps coordination
- Canary plan (DevOps):
  1) Deploy fix behind feature flag for refund handling and reconciliation changes to staging; run automated smoke and targeted E2E.
  2) Canary rollout in production to a small cohort (e.g., 5% or specific region/accounts) with feature-flag ON.
  3) Monitor refund metrics (duplicate refund count), reconciliation discrepancy, and error rates for 24-48 hours.
  4) If metrics stable and reconciliation shows 0 discrepancies in representative sample, expand to full rollout.
- DevOps tasks & estimate: deploy + canary orchestration + monitoring baseline setup — Owner: DevOps — 1 day for staging; 0.5 day for prod canary deploy + 1 day of active monitoring coordination
- Rollback considerations: flipping feature flag OFF reverts to legacy behavior immediately; if DB uniqueness constraint causes write errors on legacy traffic, DevOps should coordinate a quick redeploy and/or temporary request routing while we revert DB change. Have DB backups & migration rollback scripts ready.

6) Timeline (business days) & impact if deferred
- Parallelization: API/DB/lock work and reconciliation changes can run in parallel across 2 implementers + QA.
- Proposed timeline (conservative, parallelized):
  - Day 0.5: API idempotency RFC + Plan kickoff (Planner)
  - Days 1-3: Implement idempotency key acceptance, persist dedupe record, add lock, unit tests (Implementer)
  - Days 2-4: Implement reconciliation retry/pending-fee flow + compensating job + integration tests (Implementer/QA)
  - Days 4-5: Targeted E2E authoring & runs (BrowserTester) and CI gating configuration (CI owner)
  - Day 5: Staging deploy & canary validation run (DevOps + BrowserTester) — if staging passes, schedule prod canary
  - Day 6: Prod canary rollout + 24-48h monitoring window
- Total focused remediation timeline to reach LoopTest-ready and staging canary: ~5 business days; full safe prod canary & observation: additional 1-2 days (total ~6-7 days).

Risk/Impact if deferred
- Continued duplicate refunds -> over-refunds, customer disputes, manual reconciliations, potential financial loss and trust impact (medium-high).
- Missing fee attribution -> incorrect revenue recognition and reporting (regulatory/finance impact if persisted). Deferring increases operational overhead and risk of larger-scale payouts or accounting corrections.

7) Criteria to declare LoopTest-ready (BrowserTester re-run / acceptance)
- Automated unit & integration tests for idempotency & reconciliation pass in CI.
- Targeted E2E scenarios executed in staging with zero duplicate-refund occurrences across the test sample and correct single refund ledger entries.
- Reconciliation sample in staging shows zero discrepancies for the representative set (500 tx sample or same size as original test; aim: 0/500 or within acceptable 0.0% threshold)
- No new high/critical errors from static analysis or runtime monitoring.
- Performance: refund processing latency remains within SLA (no >20% regression on median latency) under test load.

Deliverables for this replan
- Updated design snippet (idempotency docs + dedupe ledger schema) — Planner
- Implementation PRs with unit tests — Implementer
- Integration test harness updates and E2E scenarios — QA/BrowserTester
- Staging & prod canary runbook — DevOps

Next steps (immediate)
- Orchestrator: approve replan and allocate implementer(s) & DevOps window.
- On approval: Planner will hand off idempotency design + DB change spec to Implementer and coordinate CI gating setup with QA/CI owner.

payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard‑Revenue Case

1) Scope
- Add support for a “standard revenue” data model and APIs so clients can create/read/update standard revenue entries tied to customers/products.
- Provide validations, DB migrations and backfill for existing records.
- Expose CRUD endpoints and ensure transactional safety. 
- Add automated unit/integration tests and E2E/browser tests. 
- Roll out behind a feature flag, with monitoring and rollback procedures.
- Excluded: UI redesign beyond simple form flows (unless requested separately).

2) Required data-model changes
- New table: standard_revenues
  - id (PK, uuid)
  - owner_id (FK to customer/account) or product_id depending on association model
  - revenue_type (enum: standard, promotional, other) — default 'standard'
  - amount_cents (int) or decimal(12,2) depending on currency precision
  - currency (ISO-4217 string)
  - effective_date (date) — when this standard revenue becomes active
  - expires_at (nullable date) — optional end date
  - created_by, updated_by (FK to users) and timestamps
  - status (enum: active, inactive) if soft-disable required
  - unique/indexes: (owner_id, effective_date) or business-appropriate uniqueness to prevent overlaps
- Add appropriate FK constraints and indices for queries by owner/product and by date.
- If existing revenue table exists, consider migrating recurring fields there or linking via FK.

3) API / Endpoints
- GET /v1/standard-revenues?owner_id={}&active_at={date} — list/filter
- GET /v1/standard-revenues/{id} — retrieve single
- POST /v1/standard-revenues — create (body: owner_id, amount, currency, effective_date, expires_at, revenue_type)
- PUT /v1/standard-revenues/{id} — update (same body plus optimistic locking field: version or updated_at)
- PATCH /v1/standard-revenues/{id}/status — enable/disable
- DELETE /v1/standard-revenues/{id} — soft-delete if required
- Validation responses: standard RFC-7807 style error payloads with error codes for client handling
- Auth: require scoped token with revenue:write/read permissions
- Rate limits: respect existing API policies

4) Validation rules (server-side)
- amount > 0, amount precision matches currency rules
- currency must be valid ISO-4217 code
- effective_date required and must be <= expires_at if expires_at present
- No overlapping active standard_revenues for same owner/product and overlapping date ranges (check within DB transaction)
- owner_id/product_id must exist and be accessible by caller
- For updates: optimistic concurrency (updated_at or version) to avoid lost updates
- Reject unsupported revenue_type values; provide clear error messages

5) Data migration steps
- DB schema migration: create table, indices, constraints
- Backfill plan:
  - Identify source of existing revenue info (existing revenue table or default pricing) and map fields
  - For each existing account/product, create a single standard_revenues row using current canonical revenue value and effective_date = today (or original effective date if available)
  - Run migration in batches to avoid long locks; use transaction per-batch size tuned to DB
  - Create a migration script with dry-run mode and a reversal path (delete inserted rows if rollback)
- Validate migration: row counts, sampling verification, and reconcile totals against pre-migration reports
- Take DB backup/snapshot before migration; schedule migration in low-traffic window if migration impacts indexes.

6) Automated tests
- Unit tests: model validations, business rules, overlap detection, currency precision, edge cases (leap dates, timezones if relevant)
- Integration tests: repository/DAO level (DB test DB or transactional tests) to verify migrations, uniqueness and constraints
- API tests: contract tests for each endpoint (positive & negative cases)
- Migrations tests: test-run migration against a copy of prod-like dataset (or synthetic dataset) verifying idempotency and rollback

7) E2E / Browser tests
- Paths to test:
  - Create standard revenue via API/UI, then read it back, confirm listing filters work (by owner and date)
  - Update standard revenue and verify optimistic-lock conflicts are surfaced
  - Disable/enable flow and confirm downstream calculations use the active revenue
  - Migration smoke test: after migration, verify example accounts have expected standard revenue
- Use BrowserTester to run a small suite that covers the typical UI flow + one regression test for overlapping detection

8) Roll-out strategy
- Implementation behind a feature flag (config-driven): default OFF in production
- Enable in staging and run full E2E + load tests
- Canary rollout: enable for a small subset of accounts (e.g., internal accounts or 1% sample) and monitor logs/metrics for errors, latency and data discrepancies
- Metrics to monitor: API error rate, DB lock/waits, time for create/update transactions, data reconciliation metrics (counts of migrated vs expected)
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 48–72 hours with human-in-the-loop checks
- Rollback: disable feature flag and, if needed, run DB rollback script (designed earlier) — prefer graceful disable to avoid data loss

9) Observability & monitoring
- Add structured logging for API create/update/delete with correlation IDs
- Add metrics: standard_revenues.created, standard_revenues.updated, validation.errors, migration.progress
- Alerts for increased validation errors, DB constraint violations, or rollout-induced spike in latency

10) Security & compliance
- Ensure authorization checks (owner access) on all endpoints
- Audit log entries for create/update/delete actions for compliance
- Sanitize inputs to prevent injection; use prepared statements/ORM

11) Backwards compatibility & breaking change analysis
- Non-breaking: adding new table and endpoints is additive
- Breaking risks: migrations that modify existing tables or change behavior of revenue calculations — flag these for Critic review
- Any change to existing revenue calculation must be behind feature flag until validated

12) Deployment & DevOps considerations
- DB migrations applied as part of release pipeline with migration tooling (liquibase/flyway/alembic)
- Ensure zero-downtime deployment by making DB changes additive (create new table, add columns nullable if needed)
- Deploy service changes after DB migration is confirmed successful in staging
- DevOps will deploy only after tests pass and plan approved

13) Estimated effort & timeline (calendar days, team of 1–2 engineers + QA)
- Design & Plan: 1–2 days
- Schema design & migration scripts: 2–3 days
- Backend implementation (models, services, APIs, auth): 4–6 days
- Validation & business logic (overlap checks & concurrency): 2 days
- Unit & integration tests: 2–3 days
- API contract tests & E2E test authoring: 2 days
- QA & staging verification (including migration dry-run): 2–3 days
- Rollout & monitoring (canary + ramp): 1–2 days
Total: ~16–23 business days (3–5 weeks) end-to-end. Adjust +/- based on complexity of mapping to existing revenue sources and number of owners/products.

14) Team roles / responsibilities
- Planner: finalize plan and coordinate timeline
- Reviewer: review and approve plan prior to implementation

Implementation Plan: Standard-Revenue Case

1) Scope and goals
- Implement server-side and UI support for the "standard-revenue" pricing case so that revenue calculations, reporting, and display reflect the new standard-revenue model. This includes necessary data model extensions, API additions/changes, UI updates for customers and admin, tests, migration/backfill, and deployment with rollback safety.
- Non-goals: changing legacy/non-standard revenue models, analytics pipelines outside scoped reports, external billing provider integration (unless explicitly required).

2) Assumptions
- Existing DB is relational (Postgres) with a transactions/revenue table.
- Current API is versioned; UI is a single-page app using our component library.
- We can deploy behind a feature flag.

3) Required changes
A. Data model
- Add column(s) to represent standard-revenue attributes on the revenue/transactions table (e.g., standard_revenue_amount DECIMAL NULL, revenue_type ENUM {legacy, standard}).
- Create a migration to add above columns with default NULL (additive, fast).
- Add an indexed computed/status column for quick queries if needed (e.g., is_standard_revenue boolean).
- Backfill job to populate new columns for historical data (idempotent, batched).

B. APIs
- POST/PUT endpoints that create/update revenue should accept standard-revenue fields. Update request/response schemas (v2 or additive fields in v1 with optional presence).
- Add read endpoints/augment existing GET revenue endpoints to return standard_revenue_amount and revenue_type.
- Versioning strategy: prefer additive fields in existing API for backward compatibility; if incompatible, create /v2/revenue endpoints.
- Update validation logic and business rules on the server to compute/validate standard revenue.

C. UI
- Customer-facing UI: display standard revenue where relevant (billing summary, transaction list, invoices). Add toggles/labels showing revenue type if helpful.
- Admin UI: enable creating/updating standard-revenue entries; add a report page filtered by revenue_type.
- Feature-flag UI changes to rollout gradually.

4) Step-by-step tasks (ordered, owners indicated)
Phase A — Design & Review (2-3 days)
1. Draft detailed schema changes (DB migration scripts) and API schema changes. Owner: Planner + Implementer. (0.5 day)
2. Security & breaking-change review by Reviewer/Critic. Owner: Reviewer (+ Critic if high complexity). (0.5 day)
3. Finalize plan and obtain sign-off from Orchestrator. (0.5 day)

Phase B — Implementation (3-6 days)
4. Implement DB migration (add columns, indices) and unit tests for migrations. Owner: Implementer. (0.5–1 day)
5. Implement server-side business logic: accept/validate standard-revenue fields, compute derived values. Add API contract updates and integration tests. Owner: Implementer. (1.5–2 days)
6. Implement backfill job (batched, idempotent) and test on staging subset. Owner: Implementer. (0.5–1 day)
7. Implement UI changes behind feature flag (components, display, admin controls). Owner: Implementer (frontend). (1–2 days)

Phase C — Testing (2-3 days)
8. Unit tests and automated integration tests (server + DB). Owner: Implementer/Reviewer. (0.5–1 day)
9. End-to-end tests (BrowserTester): flows for create/update/display standard revenue, reporting. Include regression tests for legacy flows. (1 day)
10. Performance test for backfill and query paths (DB load), plus small-scale load test for API changes. (0.5 day)

Phase D — Staging rollout and monitoring (1-2 days)
11. Deploy to staging behind feature flag; run full QA and testing cycles. Owner: DevOps + BrowserTester. (0.5–1 day)
12. Run backfill on staging, validate results. Owner: Implementer + QA. (0.5 day)

Phase E — Production rollout (1 day)
13. Enable feature flag for small % of traffic (canary), monitor metrics and error rates for 24 hours. Owner: DevOps + Oncall. (0.5 day + monitoring)
14. Gradually increase rollout to full population if no issues. Owner: DevOps. (0.5 day)

Total estimated engineering time: 9–15 person-days (conservative). Calendar duration: ~2–3 weeks including reviews, QA, and monitoring windows.

5) Test plan
- Unit tests: validation logic, API input/output, db migration tests.
- Integration tests: API endpoints with DB (create/read/update flow including standard_revenue fields).
- End-to-end tests: UI flows (create transaction with standard revenue, display in reports, admin edits). BrowserTester to run on staging.
- Backfill validation: record counts, checksum comparisons, sample record verification pre/post backfill.
- Performance tests: ensure queries with new columns don't regress 95th percentile response times; run backfill on replicated staging DB to measure impact.
- Security checks: ensure new fields are sanitized and access-controlled (admin-only changes where needed).
- Monitoring: error rate, latency, key business metrics (total revenue, counts), and rollout metrics.

6) Rollback strategy
- Use feature flags to disable UI and short-circuit server paths if issues arise.
- DB migrations are additive (adding nullable columns); rollback path: reverse migration to drop columns only after ensuring no code depends on them (safe only after rollback window). Primary rollback plan is to disable feature flag and revert API handlers to ignore standard_revenue fields.
- For backfill: run backfill in a reversible way (write to new columns only, keep historical values intact); to rollback, stop consumers and optionally clear written columns in batches.
- API backwards compatibility: if API v2 introduced, route clients to v1 endpoints on rollback.
- Deployment rollback: standard CI/CD rollback to previous service image; DevOps to monitor and revert if error thresholds exceeded.

7) Risk assessment & mitigations
- Risk: long-running backfill may impact DB. Mitigation: batched backfill, low priority transactions, run during off-peak windows, monitor DB metrics.
- Risk: API breaking change. Mitigation: additive fields, feature flag, versioning where necessary, reviewers to validate contract changes.
- Risk: UI inconsistency. Mitigation: feature-flagged UI, progressive rollout, manual QA.

8) Deliverables
- Migration scripts and backfill job
- Server code and API schema updates
- Frontend components and feature flag toggles
- Automated tests and test reports
- Deployment playbook and rollback runbook

9) Acceptance criteria
- All tests pass in CI and staging (unit/integration/e2e)
- Backfill completes successfully on staging and checksums match expectations
- No critical errors or performance regressions during canary rollout
- Product/PO sign-off on UI and reporting correctness

10) Communication & timeline summary
- Design & review: 2–3 days
- Implementation: 3–6 days
- Testing and staging: 2–3 days
- Production rollout and monitoring: 1–2 days
- Total: ~2–3 weeks calendar
